answer: A stake-bonded registry makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a deposit before it can earn, so spawning a thousand Sybils means locking a thousand deposits, which no fable of free abundance can fund. Honest agents build a public record, and the registry acts as a mirror, reflecting each agent's past attestations back to anyone who checks, while a haven of verified peers vouches only for identities with real stake and history, so an attacker pays full price for every mask they wear.
